utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, and good morning, everyone. First of all, I'd like to thank the Chamber for accommodating us on Monday with the scheduling so that the interview of General Abdel-Razek could take place. And I would like to ask you for one other scheduling issue, and that regards the last witness of next week that's scheduled to come, Mr. Suljevic. And by our calculations, we don't believe that there would be sufficient time during the week to complete his cross-examination. He's testifying about 17 different shelling incidents. We've asked for 20 hours of cross-examination, and it may be that the Chamber reduces that, we don't think it would be likely to be reduced to such an amount that his testimony could be concluded next week, and in that event we would prefer not to break up his cross-examination and ask that the Chamber consider advising the parties that it would not have this witness testify before the summer recess. So I wanted to alert you to that at the beginning of today's session so it can be considered. I've discussed it with Mr. Tieger, and that's our request, that we simply complete the testimony of the two witnesses, Mandilovic and Abdel-Razek, next week, and that should bring us to sometime on Wednesday and recess at that time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robinson. Mr. Tieger, at this moment I don't think we need your assistance. I was about to come to this issue. With due respect, Mr. Robinson, we have to disagree. I was about to raise that issue. The Chamber anticipates the conclusion of Mr. Mandic's evidence today and beginning the evidence of Mr. Mandilovic. Given that we have granted four hours for cross-examination of Mr. Mandilovic, his evidence should be concluded by the end of second session on Monday, when we will begin to hear the evidence of Mr. Abdel-Razek. The Chamber informed the parties yesterday that it would grant five hours for cross-examination of Mr. Abdel-Razek, which should take us to the end of the day on Tuesday. We would then start Mr. Suljevic's evidence on Wednesday, and the Chamber has applied the criteria previously set out and determined that six hours is a sufficient time for his cross-examination. We therefore anticipate being able to complete Mr. Suljevic's evidence by the end of the day on Thursday. While the precise timing remains to be seen, I would ask all the parties to do their best to ensure that we can fit within this general guide-line by not exceeding the time indicated for direct and cross-examination, and by being ready to start promptly at the beginning of each day and after the breaks. There's one further matter which concerns the evidence of Mr. Mandic. The Chamber refers to the evidence given by Mr. Mandic in the Stanisic and Zupljanin case, portions of which the accused has asked to be admitted into evidence as part of his Rule 92 ter written evidence. The Chamber notes that the Prosecution did not object to the admission of those portions identified by the accused in this manner. The Chamber has considered the accused's request, and the Chamber will admit the portions of Mr. Mandic's evidence from Stanisic and Zupljanin tendered by the accused pursuant to Rule 92 ter, which should be up-loaded into e-court and given an exhibit number. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I understood the Prosecution would have an opportunity to indicate to the Court the page -- the portions of the transcript that it considered should be admitted as well. I'm prepared to read those into the record now or take care of it at a more convenient time, as the Court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you do that in writing so that the accused can respond to that, and then the Chamber will make a ruling later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine. I would simply note there's no objection, but I would be happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: After which the one exhibit number will be given; is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And if the accused wishes to tender any of the exhibits which form an indispensable and inseparable part of the admitted portions of Mr. Mandic's testimony in Stanisic and Zupljanin, he should provide the Chamber with a list of these associated exhibits, clearly identifying where they are referred to in the relevant transcripts. In order to satisfy the indispensable and inseparable requirements, any item sought to be admitted in this manner must be one without which Mr. Mandic's testimony in Stanisic and Zupljanin would become incomprehensible or of less probative value. The Chamber will then determine whether any of these exhibits should be admitted as associated exhibits. So, Mr. Karadzic, we would ask you that you provide this list to us by the end of the day on Tuesday, 20th July. That said, we'll continue to hear the last part of cross-examination of Mr. Mandic by Mr. Karadzic. As I indicated, Mr. Karadzic, you will have two hours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everybody. Good morning, Minister.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll have to again ask for the indulgence of my learned friend and everyone in the courtroom, because I have a document we have not seen before. It was e-mailed last night to the OTP, but I'm not sure it has arrived in e-court. It's 1D2117. If we don't have it in e-court, we have two copies, one for the ELMO and one for the witness. And the purpose of the document is to see how an arrest was carried out in Zvornik, an arrest of members of the Yellow Wasps, who are listed as my co-perpetrators in the joint criminal enterprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Minister, is this a communique from the Ministry of the Interior, dated the 31st of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document in 1992, and I know about this event, when paramilitary units who had committed crimes in the Podrinje area between Zvornik and Bratunac and Bijeljina. And at your initiative and the initiative of the prime minister, in co-ordinated action, the police and the army arrested about a dozen of these men and handed them over to the competent organs. I know that this Vuckovic was tried and sentenced for a war crime. He was the leader of the Yellow Wasps, and this was one of the first actions of the legal organs of the government, the state, against paramilitary units who did not want to subordinate themselves to the military command.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted and marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D480, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, that they resisted arrest and that they were armed, so that a special-purpose unit had to be used which arrived from Pale?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know all about this because the government received a report of this event. I know that some looted property was found in the possession of these people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at 1D2118. If it has not arrived in e-court, I hope everybody has a translation. Could you just give the document to Mr. Mandic, and there is a translation which I hope everybody has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I confirm that the Bench has the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, that these were Serbian citizens and that we extradited them to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the first time I've seen the indictment, but I do know they underwent trial very soon in the Republic of Serbia because they were citizens of Serbia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the highlighted parts?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an indictment launched with the District -- rather, lodged by the District Attorneys' Office against Dusko Vuckovic and Vojin Vuckovic, also known as Zuco, and I think the Yellow Wasps were named after him. And from April to June 1992, on the territory of Zvornik municipality in the former Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as members of the Igor Markovic Unit, which was part of the Zvornik Municipality TO War Staff during the civil war in the former Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, they violated international law by killing, inflicting bodily injuries on, and torturing the civilian population. And then the dates are mentioned. The crimes are described as a war crime against the civilian population. This was a federal law, so the Penal Code of the FRY applied, whereas rape is a republican -- is a crime of the republican law, so the law of Serbia was applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at page 5 and read out the highlighted part?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The accused, Dusko Vuckovic, stated in his Defence that he really cut off the ear of a Muslim, that he fired shots from an automatic rifle in the cultural centre in Celopek, and as far as he remembers, he killed seven or eight people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as far as he remembers, he killed seven or eight people, but: "He claims he never forced (redacted) to have sexual intercourse with him and that he did not take 1.000 German marks from her."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The prosecutor did not believe him?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the prosecutor thought he was simply trying to lessen his responsibility.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the name of the victim be redacted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you read the highlighted part of the last page?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It is proposed that the detention of the accused Dusko Vuckovic be extended until the trial is concluded because the accused committed three serious criminal offences which upset the public and because a sentence of 10 years' imprisonment is prescribed for each of the offences. The release of the accused Dusko during the trial would upset the public even more, which could affect the peaceful course of the criminal proceedings."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And they did not release him, did they?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not release him until the final sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did the local leadership have sufficient reason, in view of the fact that they received complaints against these people, and we at Pale also received complaints against them, to warn the citizens that they could not guarantee their safety until such time as these renegade elements were brought under control?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only speculate, but I assume that this was one of the reasons that the safety of the population could not be guaranteed, because the local authorities were unable to control these renegade units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that the Muslims returned to Kozluk alive and well, almost all of them, and that nothing bad happened to them? Yes, they went to Subotica and then on to European countries, but as soon as the war was over, they came back, and now they live in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place where there is the greatest number of returnees, the two places, are Janja and Kozluk on the territory of the Republika Srpska, and I know that they have built two or three houses of worship and that many Muslims now live and work in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, Mr. Mandic, I didn't follow your statement that these Vuckovic brothers, they did not -- they were not released -- I strike that. I quote you: "They did not release him until the final sentence." So did you mean that they were released at the time of their sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they are still in prison, Your Honours. I think that one of them has even died, had a heart attack. They were never released, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you, by any chance, know how this trial ended up, the conclusion of this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, we have the sentence -- the judgement. The next document is the judgement, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Because you moved to another topic, I intervened. Thank you. I apologise. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D481, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but as since we are still discussing the pre-trial stage in relation to this group, can we have 1D2119. Unfortunately, we don't have the translation. It's the judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So would you kindly read us the statement of reasons in the judgement, the highlighted part? The Registry has this copy of the judgement. It's 2119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's in e-court. And in the meantime, until the redacted version will be offered, 1D -- no, the Exhibit D481, this indictment will be put under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person did not ask to be protected, but my feeling is that the name should be kept from the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister -- we have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the final judgement of the Supreme Court of Serbia, following an appeal by the accused and the OTP, and Dusan Vuckovic is sentenced to eight years and six months in prison. That's for committing a war crime against the civilian population from Article 142(1) of the Penal Code of the Republic of Yugoslavia, and a prison sentence of two years for the crime of rape, Article 103(1) of the Penal Code of the Republic of Serbia. [In English] Could you lift the page a little bit. Now they don't see anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As a lawyer, I think Mr. Mandic is able to sum up the crux of the judgement, and we can read the judgement later on. We can move expeditiously in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dusan Vuckovic was found guilty of several crimes, and an amalgamated sentence of 10 years was handed down. And the time he spent in custody has been credited to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page 10 in Serbian. And as we are talking about a crime --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, it should reach "Dusko" instead of "Dusan"; correct, Mr. Mandic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: If I may, this is a usual hypocorism for "Dusan," when you call Dusan "Dusko."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, the Appeals Court is giving the grounds as to why the prison sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: In English: "The fact ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go on. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Court of Appeal has increased the prison sentence of this Dusko because they felt that the Trial Chamber gave too much weight to mitigating circumstances; that he had a young child, that he had been captured by the Muslims and tortured. But they did not give sufficient weight to aggravating circumstances, which is that the victims were civilians, and this was an especially aggravating circumstance for the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Article in English, please, because Dr. Kovacevic is mentioned in this and in Serbian version is not. Okay, anyway, if the participants are satisfied, we can end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D482, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, a witness here, an expert, said that the commander in Banja Luka had told him that he would disarm paramilitaries. That witness was actually misled by other people that it would be the Muslim paramilitaries that would be disarmed. Do you agree that the SOS are Serb paramilitaries and that they were disarmed? So if the SOS were disarmed, it is a case of disarming Serbs, not Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SOS are Serb paramilitary units. I know about that. I don't know anything about that disarming, though.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the permission of the Trial Chamber, we are going to tender those documents as well about the disarming of Serbs in the area around Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, had we been granted all the time we had asked for, we could have clarified all these matters, but now I'd like to draw your attention to something. I don't know how good you are at geography, but this map shows the borders of municipalities. So could I please have in e-court map number 2070123 [as interpreted] from the batch that is called "The Karadzic Court Binder." Perhaps the distinguished Mr. Tieger knows the actual number in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is that number --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, if that number could be repeated. I don't think that's a correct recitation of the number. There's a few too much digits, for one thing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the second map in this binder, and there's this red number here, "0701-0723."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That should help, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, map number 2 in that binder.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Yes, that's the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, may I ask you to start from the south -- the south-east, rather. Can you indicate the municipality of Trebinje, which is a predominantly-Serb municipality, purely Serb, as we say in our language?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Before the war, that is to say, in 1991, Trebinje had a majority Serb population. 20-something per cent of the population were Muslim and about 5 or 6 per cent were others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I happen to know the composition of that population because I worked in the police force and we had this information about all municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In our language, when we say "purely Serb," it doesn't mean Serb-cleansed, it means predominantly Serb; way over 50 per cent, let's put it that way?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly over two-thirds of the population Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Ljubinje right next to it, and is Ljubinje also over 50 per cent Serb?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, do you see the municipality of Stolac? Do you know where the former municipality of Berkovic is that belongs to Stolac?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the road between Bileca and Stolac. I'm going to mark it here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it remained in Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a newly-formed municipality, Berkovici. It exists to this day. Yes, it's in the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, I give the microphone to you now, and could you tell us about these municipalities in Stari Herzegovina, like Foca and others? We had an MP from Foca, though. And could you mark the front-line, to the best of your recollection? I don't expect it to be absolutely precise. No one could expect that. But we would like the Trial Chamber to see what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trebinje -- well, we are talking about the population and the composition of municipalities on the eve of the war in 1991. Trebinje was a predominantly-Serb town, as well as Ljubinje, Bileca, Gacko, Nevesinje, Kalinovik. Foca was 51 per cent -- or, rather, 50-something per cent Muslim populated and 49 per cent Serb populated. It was sort of half/half, as far as Foca was concerned. So this was a split municipality, if we look at population figures only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this part below Foca, is that Eastern Herzegovina? The SAO Eastern Herzegovina, did it consist of these municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you already moved on to the SAO of Stari Herzegovina? Actually, I don't know whether they had established an SAO, but Kalinovik, Foca, Gorazde, Rudo and Cajnice is Stari Herzegovina, isn't it, and Visegrad too?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gorazde had a predominantly-Muslim population. Visegrad also had a predominantly-Muslim population. Rudo and Cajnice were predominantly Serb populated. That is what I had put a circle around. Rogatica, predominantly Muslim populated. Sokolac, Serb population. Pale, also predominantly Serb populated. [Marks] However, the municipality of Pale belonged to the city of Sarajevo. It was the 10th municipality within the city of Sarajevo. Srebrenica was predominantly Muslim populated. Han Pijesak is SAO Romanija, predominantly Serb populated. Zvornik -- Zvornik, Bratunac and Srebrenica, Podrinje, was predominantly Muslim populated. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you use a blue marker now to show East Herzegovina, Stari Herzegovina, and Birac, as three regions, so that the Trial Chamber would understand what we mean when speaking about those regions?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Herzegovina, the region of Eastern Herzegovina. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you put an E and H there, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now Stari Herzegovina, Old Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stari Herzegovina, Old Herzegovina [marks]. However, Foca was also included in Old Herzegovina. So this is Stari Herzegovina. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Birac? Also, I think Visegrad was also included in Stari Herzegovina, if I remember correctly, but then you would --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the pre-war situation. However, during the course of the war, of course, Visegrad became included in that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "Stari Grad" means "Old Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You put an "SH" there, so could you put an "OH" there instead? Right. Birac includes Zvornik, Vlasenica, and Sekovici, I believe, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Birac. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Birac. Could you please identify the SAO of Semberija and Majevica?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Semberija, Majevica, Bijeljina, Lopare.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Ugljevik?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and Ugljevik. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Semberija and Majevica. Please could you please indicate the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and while you're marking it, could you tell us who lives there and what the ratio is?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SAO Krajina was composed of Drvar, Mrkonjic, Skender Vakuf, all of this. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's part of Krupa, too, so look at the River Una, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Krupa, Novi and Kostunica up there, so the River Una; right? Do you agree that in Bosanska Grahovo, almost 100 per cent of the population was Serb?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs had an absolute majority in Petrovac, in Drvar, in Grahovo. That is the so-called Visoko Krajina, the High Krajina. The population was mainly involved in livestock production. It was a mountainous area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Bosansko Grahovo, Livanjsko Polje, Glamoc, Sipovo, and Kljuc, could you include all of that? It's not Jajce, though, no, no. Just part of that field there? Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, you've taken too much of Livno. So this is invalid, if you could mark it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's a way you can delete it, Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now mark Doboj, Derventa, Modrica, where there were relative Serb majorities and there were some villages that we're going to look at on another map, but, anyway, could you mark that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Doboj [marks]. This is Modrica [marks]. Here's Derventa [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now part of the municipalities of Brod, Orasje, Obudovac, et cetera, and there's a link up there; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you just put "NB" there standing for "North Bosnia."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please initial this, and could you put the date there? Oh, yes, sorry, Romanija, could you mark the Sarajevo Romanija region? What was that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sokolac, Han Pijesak. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Put an "SR" there, "Sarajevo Romanija."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the date now, and then your initials, and then we're going to ask for the next map.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "BK" would mean "Bosnian Krajina" or "Bosanski Krajina"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. However, I'm not very good at this. I'm not very good at drawing, Your Honours. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is Cazinska Krajina, to the north of the letters BK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Was that saved? Did we give that a number? Let's give it a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D483.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we admit the unmarked version as well, just in case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The un-annotated version will be Exhibit D484.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 0724, the next one. 5225 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, you've confirmed that this 1991 census was never verified in the Assembly. We discussed that, didn't we? Do you agree that that census was never verified and that the 1981 consensus [as interpreted] was considered to be more accurate?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We in the police force did use the 1991 census, Mr. President, when we were appointing commanders, chiefs, and other top personnel in the police force. Now, whether the Assembly admitted this or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the next map in the same binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have the 65 ter number of the map from map 3?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D225, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's already D225, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The transcript said "5225." Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must have misspoken. D225.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, while we're looking at Bosansko Grahovo, Glamoc -- yes, that's right. Do you find this map familiar?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a map of the ethnic composition of Bosnia-Herzegovina, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the colour blue goes to the Una River, so that is part of Bihac, half of Bosanska Krupa, almost all of Bosanski Novi? If you do remember, could you please draw the separation lines in relation to this colour? Perhaps you could use the colour red, since this is blue. Do you agree that the front-line was on the Una River?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. I know the front-line was on the Una River, but I can hardly draw the separation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, start from the area south of Bihac. Try to delineate the ethnically Serb areas.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which years?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the beginning. However, we lost something at the end, but we'll deal with that later.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Start drawing as it was at the beginning of the war. Along the Una River, I believe we held all that, and Grahovo as well.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the Bosnian Krajina, isn't it, the lower and the upper part?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this covered the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The area around Doboj -- Trebava and Doboj is Serb majority, and south of Doboj is Ozren?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is Mountain Ozren. Population lived from livestock production, mainly. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then Uzice. Trebava is in the area of Modrica, it's a concentration of Serbs. And now the front-line did not include Gradacac, but it did cover all these Serbian territories. If you remember where the front-line was, draw it, please, all the way to Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's a rather broad stroke. Can you go back to the east, to Serb territories? We didn't even hold all of Zvornik. The area north of Zvornik, we didn't hold.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, then, that most of Trebinje, all of Ljubinje and part of Stolac, including Berkovici, all of Nevesinje, and a good part of Prenj, looking from below upwards, and then we go back. Boracko Lake towards Sarajevo, we held all that. Now, that bit we did not control. You have to go to the right, above Zvornik. We didn't even hold Teocak, nor the Tursan hill. We did have Sekovici, though, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Sekovici was an absolute Serb majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We didn't hold Kalesija, nor this green part of Zvornik. Sapna, Kovacevic, those were areas where the concentration of Muslims --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's good. But now we would have to go almost up to Brcko. There was like a connection of less than 10 kilometres. Just follow the Serb areas.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now if you can connect -- Orasje was a Serb area, and later we controlled Odjak and all of Brod.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your last statement was not translated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We couldn't hear it. The microphone is either too far away or switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you, Minister, to write today's date and your initials. And write "LC" or "CL" for "Confrontation Line."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is all very proximate and rough. We'll have a precise map. Can we save this and upload the same map again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that: Mr. Mandic, did you delete some part of the line which is near Doboj? Is it completed or -- I remember you deleted some part of it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can mention, Gracanica and Gracac were not under our control. You should follow the line. Ozren was purely Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You remember that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this hook below "Ozren," just delineate our territories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, only when you confirm what Mr. Karadzic is saying -- you just draw, but just draw as far as you know, just not following the instruction of Mr. Karadzic. Or if you don't know, you can say you don't know the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask where Gracanica and Gracac are under our control or not? Look north of Ozren.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gracanica and Gracac were not ours. They always belonged to the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you adjust this north line above Ozren accordingly?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, it's almost there. I think you should also erase the line east of Ozren.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Despite the Court's guidance, I'm watching Mr. Mandic's face. He's shrugging and making facial gestures that I think clearly signal some discomfiture with the process. I think he needs to be -- you've asked him to confirm. Mr. Karadzic quickly interceded and asked him then to re-mark the map. I think it's going to be very difficult for you to know what it is the witness knows about the designations he's been instructed to put on the map and what he doesn't, unless some effort is made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was observing the same, but I took it to mean that he is not good at drawing. But, Mr. Mandic, could you clarify? Could you answer to the observation of Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly where these municipalities in Northern Bosnia are located, and I'm really not familiar with these frontiers held during the war by Serbs, Muslims, or Croats. I know that most of these territories, Krajina and Visoka were held throughout the war by the Serbs, and the entire eastern part of Herzegovina, which relies on the Drina River and the Sava River facing Croatia. That's all I know. I'm really very bad at geography and I can't deal with maps. I suggest Mr. Karadzic bring an officer here. There's a very good officer, Subotic, in Banja Luka, who can help you with that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, although this is not precise, I would like to tender this, because it is -- I mean, for what it's worth, Gracac and -- [indiscernible] and Gracac were really not ours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The marked map will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The annotated map will be Exhibit D485.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am embarrassing myself here, really, with this map, and Muslims and Croats will hold it against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We also lost in the war and we never got back Grahovo, Glamoc, and Drvar, Petrovac, municipalities that were almost 100 per cent Serb, and also Kljuc, which was a majority-Serb town?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that under the Dayton Accords, the entire High Krajina were given to the federation, whereas before the war, in 1991, and even today, I believe, this is an area with a majority-Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The indictment alleges that I told members of the Parliament about these municipalities in Eastern Bosnia, that we had grabbed for ourselves certain municipalities where we were not in the majority. I'm trying to say that I was trying to heal thereby the wounds of those MPs who hailed from these eastern municipalities where we were a majority.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you say that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I say at an Assembly session that we got or we grabbed for ourselves certain municipalities where we were not the majority, does it correlate with the fact that we had lost certain municipalities where we were almost 100 per cent a majority?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that at these Assembly sessions, the MPs were insatiable. I believe they had taken half of Serbia and half of Croatia. It still wouldn't have been enough for them. But you did try to explain these war strategies, but I don't know anything about it. I really can't help you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's okay. I'll put this question to a politician, then. Can we get the Cutileiro map, 0780, the first draft, which was, in principle, accepted by the Serbs. 0701-0780, or 59 -- marked "59" in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. 19151. Sorry, maybe there's a -- I don't know if it was heard correctly. 19151 is the one that appears not to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that this served Mr. Cutileiro in drawing his own map? We were given the entire border at the Una, but this was his draft. Can you show Podrinje, Bratunac, Vlasenica, Srebrenica, and most of Zvornik was planned to be part of the Muslim entity, and we accepted that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the basis of the Cutileiro Plan. I remember that, and I knew about this. But for the Court and for the OTP, I will mark the municipalities with a majority-Muslim population that the Cutileiro Plan accorded to the Serbian entity. That's Vlasenica, Srebrenica, and this bit of Podrinje and Zvornik. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the original proposal, this was supposed to be part of the Muslim entity, and we accepted that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that our proclamation to these people -- our appeal to them not to fight made sense because it could have gone to their entity, even without any war, or, rather, had there not been a war?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the Sarajevo Agreement, this was to be part of the Muslim entity. I don't know anything about proclamations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I draw your attention to the area of Sarajevo. Pale, Sarajevo proper, and Ilijas, was this marked as an area with prominent Serb majority? There was only a small part of Sarajevo without a Serb majority?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you about all the 10 municipalities and their ethnic composition before the war. Han Pijesak, majority Serb; Sokolac, majority Serb; Pale, also. Novo Sarajevo was majority Serb, and Ilijas. Majority Muslim municipalities: Centar, Stari Grad, Ilidza, Hadzici, and Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll bring another map. Can you just confirm that all the three parties accepted that the three ethnic entities did not have to have contiguous territories?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, and it was approved by the mediators.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should Mr. Mandic initial this, although he didn't make any markings, and then we can tender it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll just admit the clean version of this map. We don't have to mark it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D486, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have been briefly left without any support. I would now like to see the ethnic map of Sarajevo. Just a moment, please. I'm sure you're able to show us the Sarajevo area on the ethnic map and the demarcation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the municipality of Ilidza, as can be seen here, was rather long and that Hrasnica was the Muslim part of Ilidza, whereas the Serbian part was to the north-west?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indigenous Serbs lived in Ilidza who had land around the River Bosna, whereas Hrasnica was a village or a neighbourhood with the majority Muslim population. I know this personally because I grew up there. My parents lived there for more than 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that Sokolovic Kolonija was built mostly for people from Sandzak and that it became synonymous with those buildings erected to attract people from Sandzak to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was built on water reservoirs, without any permission from the town planning authorities, and that it was settled by mostly people of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Sanac, Sokolje, Hrasno Brdo, parts of Buca, Potok and Bujakov Potok were also illegal settlements built, without any plan or approval, mostly by people from Sandzak?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with "Vox" magazine?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Vox" magazine was published by an acquaintance of mine from Foca. I know him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us his name?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sahinpasic, also known as Saja. He is a good friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was one of the main suppliers of weapons to the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a real businessman, a trader, yes, he did trade in weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that he was a prominent member of the Party of Democratic Action and the deputy of that party?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Saja was an associate of Mr. Izetbegovic, a close friend of his, and he was at the top -- among the top leadership of the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us his name and nickname slowly, for the sake of the record?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name is Senad, Saja.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, could you repeat the name for the benefit of us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sahinpasic, Senad. Senad is the first name, also known as Saja.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sahinpasic, and it's all one word. Sahinpasic is his last name, and Senad is his first name, and S-a-j-a, Saja, nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If in "Vox" they announced very soon they would be building Sokolovic Kolonija, how would you interpret this?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sahinpasic liked alarming the Serbs through that newspaper of his. He liked printing extremist viewpoints, to the detriment of the Serbs. I had occasion to read his newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that this was a threat to the effect that a second Sokolovic Kolonija would be built and that the place would be settled by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's look at the ethnic map. Do you agree that at Ilidza, which you know well, the Serbs controlled the Serbian parts of Ilidza and the Muslims controlled Hrasnica, Sokolovic Kolonija and Butmir?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was precisely these neighbourhoods that had a majority Muslim population, Butmir, Sokolovic Kolonija and Hrasnica, and they were contiguous. Looking towards Mount Igman, to the right, the majority population was Serbian. This was the indigenous population. They were farmers. They had held that land for centuries. The last names were Djokic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Jokic, Krkar [phoen], and so on, yes. Do you agree, or do you know, or is there any evidence showing that we had any intention of taking that part of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, at the beginning of the war there was a problem at Ilidza, because from Sokolovic Kolonija they were constantly launching attacks and firing shells, attacking the central part of Ilidza. While I was at Lukavica, in Sarajevo, I'm not aware there were ever any plans to enter those territories which had a majority Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is there something here that has not been admitted? Can this map be admitted or has it already been admitted? D, it's been admitted. May we now have 1D1969.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I tell you, Minister, that this is a view from Mount Hum, would you find this credible? That's picture number 1. You lived in Sarajevo, you know it well, so is this a view from Mount Hum?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the repeater.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who controlled Hum throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim Army. The BH Army, that is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have picture 5 from this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Novo Sarajevo or New Sarajevo down there, and further on is Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate -- well, very well. It's gone now. We'll do that later. Do you agree that this is a view from Mount Hum in the direction of Mount Trebevic? So Mount Hum is opposite Mount Trebevic, and Sarajevo lies in between?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Hum. There's the repeat on Trebevic [marks]. And here's the Avaz skyscraper which has been built in Sarajevo. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate Grbavica and the Jewish cemetery, if you can see it from here --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Holiday [marks], this is the Assembly and the government, so the Jewish cemetery should be around here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it to the right of the Assembly of the government? I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Vrbanja Most, the bridge, and then to the left is the Jewish cemetery. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you mark Trebevic with a T?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is the repeater at Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you identify Debelo Brdo? Is it to the right, above these two small circles? Is that Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this here? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you point out Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the area of Grbavica on this picture?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the area of Grbavica. Maybe you've gone too far into Hrasno. But can you mark Grbavica with a G?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Mr. President, are we talking about Grbavica, regardless of who held it in the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Can you mark in blue where we held it, up to what line our territory extended?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have point 17 so that we can see -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put a date there and your initials, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you put "DB" where Debelo Brdo is?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll separately admit this marked photo, which is page 5 of this exhibit, separately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D487, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 17 from this exhibit, picture 17. Picture 17 from this batch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's some technical difficulty. I suggest to have a break now, and then after the break it will be sorted out. Half an hour. We'll resume at ten to 11.00. I should correct. Five to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you will have 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Just one quick housekeeping matter. We won't be offering any associated exhibits from the Stanisic and Zupljanin case. We've used all of those that we wished to. And we also don't have any objection to whichever portions of the transcript that the Prosecutor will seek to add to our submission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We appreciate that, Your Honour. We anticipate providing associated exhibits, and I imagine that was contemplated by the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Can we have picture 17 of 1D1969 just so that Mr. Mandic can identify something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this again is a view from Hum, but in the direction of the old town, the eastern part of town?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the Breka neighbourhood, and you can also see Vratnik, yes, the old part of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what we see in the foreground, is that the neighbourhood of Velesici?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the houses you can see there, the family houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put a Latin letter V there to indicate Velesici, and can you also mark Bascarsija and the other parts of the old town that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the old town. Is this the slope of Mount Kosevo in the direction of Velesici?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Breka [marks], this new settlement here, new neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, mark it as Breka. And what did you mean by these two letters?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "BS" with a diacritic, that's Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with "OC" for "Old City"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see where the entrance to the tunnel to Mount Kosevo is from the Velesici side?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark, on Trebevic, where Osmice is, if you can't mark in my previous question?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What would you say what is the difference between Breka and Osmice, as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put an "O" for "Osmice"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between three and five, not less than three; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, as the crow flies, but along the road it's seven or eight kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What we see there is that the military hospital -- no, it's the government building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate where the government and the Assembly buildings are? I think I can see them.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Holiday Inn [indicates], and that's the Assembly building. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark them with letters? Sorry, can you mark the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well. And could you put an "A" for "Assembly," or "G" for "Government"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if there's anything else you recognise -- do you see where the Jajce Barracks is to the east?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's up there at the entrance to Stari Grad or the Old City. This is the way from Pale to the old part of Sarajevo. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, can you put "BJ" for "Barracks Jajce."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you put your initials and the date, please, on this picture?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted separately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D488, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D1970, picture 3, please. I apologise to the interpreters and everybody else. I'm not very good under time pressure, when I want to show as much as I can. 1D1970. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a view from the Jajce Barracks?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Bembasa here, the Bembasa swimming pools.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark this? I see the library, the Church of St. Anthony, the sawmill, the cemetery. Colina Kapa, I think, is on the horizon, and Debelo Brdo, and I've forgotten what the pointed peak is to the right of Debelo Brdo. But can you tell us all the things you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the Bembasa ponds, the entrance to the old part of Sarajevo. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with a "P"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the tallest buildings, and the library. Can you mark it with a "L" for "Library"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Toma Masaryk skyscraper opposite to Skenderija [indicating].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you mark skyscraper with an "S. And the Church of St. Anthony, where is that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can put "S" for "St. Anthony."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see Debelo Brdo to the left?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Debelo Brdo, "DB." [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And to the top of the horizon, do you see Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the cemetery at Kovaci. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Alifakovac, that's the same thing?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And Alifakovac is up there, Mr. President. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the thing you circled, can you mark it with an "A," "AC," "Alifakovac Cemetery"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark Colina Kapa? Is that the great Colina Kapa, because there's the lesser Colina Kapa a bit lower down? Can you just mark it with a "CK "with a diacritic on the C?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell Their Honours who held the Jajce Barracks throughout that period?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Jajce Barracks was always held by the Muslim forces, the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put a date and your signature on this map?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when it is admitted, I would like to see picture 7 from this exhibit. Is this admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admit. Picture number 3 of 1D1970 will be admitted as Exhibit D489.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, who was at Debelo Brdo and who was at Colina Kapa? Throughout the war, who held Colina Kapa and Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could I have picture number 7. Obviously, the transcript doesn't reflect the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that is what you said; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have picture 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Minister, that this picture was taken from the same position and that it shows the remainder of the city, the Unis Skyscraper, the military hospital, the government building, Vijecnica town hall, everything else you can identify?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Hum [marks]. This is the Hum repeater, and those photographs that we looked at a moment ago were taken from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sorry, can we have the letter H there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is the repeater at Hum [marks]. This is the government building [marks]. These are the Unis Skyscrapers at Marin Dvor. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you place "G" for "Government and "U" for "Unis"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the new Avaz building [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It didn't exist before the war, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a new one. That's why it's a bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you identify the military hospital?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here's the military hospital [marks]. Here's the town hall, Vijecnica [marks]. This is the area of the old city, or, rather, Bascarsija, all of it. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "OC," can you place "OC" for "Old City"? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vijecnica, just put an "L" for "Library."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Down here to the left is Miljacka. Here is Debelo Brdo. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Mezari, or, rather, the Muslim cemetery, this over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The river, could you mark it with an arrow and put an "M" there or, "R," rather, for "River"? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, from here and from Hum, can one target practically any point in town?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not a military expert, really. You're asking me things from Mr. Subotic's field, and the man isn't doing a thing in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. I take that into account. But do you agree that they are at Colina Kapa, Hum, the Jajce Barracks?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have already established that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the date and your initials?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for our purpose, what did you write for "Military Hospital"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "B," the letter B.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put "M" above that, "Military Hospital"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D490, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D1971, please. Picture 12, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you agree that this is the view from Mojmilo, facing the south, Dobrinja, et cetera? Can you identify it for us, actually, what we can see from here? Do you agree that this is the view from Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please identify these compounds here?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hrasnica [marks]. This is the airport [marks] and the neighbourhood of Butmir to the right. It can't really be seen properly. Then there is Mount Igman. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Bjelasnica is the white thing we can see up here?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, behind Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, can we erase this and can we identify Igman and Bjelasnica? Actually, we didn't need to erase that. Could you mark Igman and Bjelasnica separately?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Igman. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Bjelasnica, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Bjelasnica. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So red "I" is "Igman" and the blue letter "B" is "Bjelasnica"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's why it's called Bjelasnica, because it's mostly covered with snow. You can see that it's covered with snow, even when this picture was taken. It's spring-time, isn't it? You can see that it is spring-time and there's snow on Bjelasnica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of the other participants, "bijelo" is white, so Bjelasnica is white.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So could you mark "B," "Butmir"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Hrasnica is at the very foot of Mount Igman. That's where I lived for 15 years. This is the airport [marks], and underneath the airport is Butmir, a neighbourhood with a predominantly Muslim population. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber who held positions at Bjelasnica, Igman, and Mojmilo, the viewpoint from which this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war, it was held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; the Muslims, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These neighbourhoods, these blocks of flats, can you identify them for us?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, this is Olimpijsko Naselje, the Olympic neighbourhood, Mojmilo, Vojnicko Polje and Dobrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Lukavica; can you discern it up there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Lukavica [marks]. Now it's called Eastern Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you place the letter "L" there, just an "L," sorry, not "EL."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, these neighbourhoods down here, can you identify them one by one and just mark them? And please speak into the microphone so that it is reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Vojnicko Polje [marks]. This is Mojmilo [marks]. This is Dobrinja [marks]. This is Dobrinja as well [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put the date and your initials there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D491, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have picture 23 from here. It would be instructive if this entire bunch of photographs could be admitted, because the Trial Chamber could see properly what all of this is about. 23, please. 23 from the same number, could I please have that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, the last page of this bunch. It's coming.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly. Is there any hope? We have it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, can you recognise the point where this photograph was taken and what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the neighbourhood of Alipasino Polje, viewed from Mojmilo, from Milinkladska, but a bit further up towards Vraca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark Alipasino Polje for us and also all those neighbourhoods up there in the hills?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is the repeater from Hum. This is Hum. This is Alipasino Polje [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put "AP" there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise Boljakov Potok, and what else, Brijesce, Buca Potok? Can you recognise any of that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Boljakov Potok, this is Buca Potok. This is Brijesce down here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Boljakov Potok as well?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. And what about Buca?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Buca [marks]. This is Hum down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you agree that these neighbourhoods are well known for having been built without any building permits? Therefore, the ethnic structure of the population of Sarajevo was changed artificially because these people moved in from Sandzak?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These neighbourhoods were built up without any building permits or without any plans, and it is mostly people from Serbia who moved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Muslims from Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, ethnic Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Brijesce, Buca Potok, Boljakov Potok?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here they are. Brijesce, Boljakov Potok. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put the date there and your initials?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you, Minister, that in this neighbourhood several incidents took place and the Serbs are being blamed for that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you spell this out in specific terms; before the war? When? After the multi-party elections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no. During the war, there are different explosions there in water lines, at sports stadiums, et cetera. It's a rather densely-populated neighbourhood. Predominantly Muslims lived there, because Serbs had fled. Did you hear of different incidents that took place there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D492, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Minister, we tried to play this footage. However, it is barely audible. Nevertheless, the OTP succeeded and they managed to get it. 1D2090, could we have that, please. Actually, sorry, can we have Colina Kapa as well. I'd like to see another photograph. Can we have 1D1967, please. Picture 7 from this number, 1D1967. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, do you agree that this is the view from Colina Kapa, a view of Sarajevo from Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Hum repeater. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is the view from the southern side, from the hill of Trebevic, facing the north?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is from Osmice, towards Trebevic, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Colina Kapa, who was at Colina Kapa throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colina Kapa, to the best of my knowledge, was held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the road was from Trebevic to Sarajevo and back to Trebevic.
